resources.string: Very high CPU load. Motion-compensated 2× deinterlacing using Snow internally (no output encoding). TFF: top field first; BFF: bottom field first. Fixed field order, always processed; only use on matching interlaced material. May be too slow for live TV.
Automatic · variable load
Low load · simpler picture
Balanced · moderate load
Smoother motion · double frame rate
Special methods · read the notes
Film · inverse telecine
The backend chooses the method. Cost and output frame rate depend on its choice; this does not guarantee hardware deinterlacing.
Very low load. Discards one field; reduces vertical detail and motion resolution.
Very low load. Averages field lines; reduces vertical detail and motion resolution.
Low load. Blends fields; moving objects can show ghosting.
Low algorithm cost, double output frame rate (50i → 50p). Smooth motion, but fine lines may flicker.
Moderate CPU load. Motion-adaptive deinterlacing at the input frame rate (50i → 25p).
Higher CPU load. Motion-adaptive deinterlacing with both fields (50i → 50p); useful for sport.
Moderate CPU load. Three-field interpolation. The 2× variant preserves both motion phases and increases processing load.
High CPU load. Edge-directed interpolation; the 2× variant doubles output frames. Test on your device.
Very high CPU load, even with Vulkan output. Neural interpolation (16 neurons); 2× costs more. May be too slow for HD live TV. Separate from the NNEDI3 upscaler.
Legacy CPU filter, moderate load. Fixed field order; unsuitable if motion judders. Prefer BWDIF for automatic field-order detection.
Moderate load, double frame rate. Simulates CRT field decay; may leave motion trails. VLC can substitute another method for unsupported pixel formats.
Film with 3:2 pulldown only (29.97 → 23.976 fps), not ordinary 50i/60i live video. Moderate to high load. Incorrect use causes judder.
Low to moderate load. VLC spatial interpolation; limited pixel-format support can cause VLC to substitute a method.
CPU filters require readable frames (copy-back), including with Vulkan output. Hardware decoding may remain active. Load estimates vary with device and resolution.
VLC filter selection is not a SoC hardware-deinterlacing selector. Decoder, pixel format and output determine the usable path. Load estimates vary by device.
Low performance mode currently uses %1$s. Your selected method remains saved.
The selected deinterlacing method could not be applied. Try Auto or another method.
